personas: Parent on a phone or iPad

journeys.name: Wake the screen and see Home

steps.text: Touch the sleeping screen: it wakes, and the touch does not press the button under it.
Home shows the clock, date, weather, next event and the wave background.
Move between destinations by tap or swipe; collapse the nav rail for a full-screen view.
Count down to a family date on Home.
Every screen still renders from saved copies when the network drops.

journeys.name: Kid does a Star Job and a habit, earns stars, undoes a mistake

steps.text: Pick my name with the avatar switcher.
Tap a Star Job: it shows pending at once and a star flies to the jar, with sound.
Tap a habit; finishing every habit earns a star.
Undo a mistaken tap within 10 seconds and the star comes back off.
A tap the server refuses reverts with a gentle message.
Finish everything: the all-done banner shows once per day.
Watch the goal jar fill toward the reward I picked.
Games and Music wait until today's jobs are done, or a grown-up unlocks them.
An any-day job sits under This week until done.
Six Star Jobs and six habits fit the wall without scrolling the page.
Open a routine from the kid's board, including a kid who has only routines.
Step through it, reload to resume, and see the celebration at the end.
A step tapped offline survives a reload and is saved once back online.
The header badge shows pending Star Jobs and leads to the PIN, then Approvals.
Approve one or all; the star turns gold on the wall.
Send a job back with a note, and no stars are paid.
Give or remove bonus stars with a note; the kid sees the bonus celebration.
Undo an approved job any time later.
Read the weekly summary for each child.
A failed approve puts the row back with a message.

journeys.name: Kid spends stars in the reward shop

steps.text: Browse the shop and make a reward my goal.
Reach the goal: the header badge counts it for grown-ups.
Get it now: preview, then the PIN.
A grown-up redeems; the stars come off and it is logged.
A failed redeem puts the stars back.
Earn a badge: it celebrates once and fills the kid's sticker book.
A grown-up sets an allowance rate; the kid cashes out and the parent marks it paid.

journeys.name: Family calendar: today, week, add an event

steps.text: Agenda shows today with members and location; a tap opens details.
Week and month views show timed, spanning and all-day events; swipe changes the period.
Filter the calendar by member.
Add an event from the wall or a phone; it shows pending, then confirmed.
Edit or delete an event; a conflict rolls back.
Connect a calendar link or Google and see its health.
The now line follows the time; the view is remembered.
The calendar fits phone and tablet screens.

journeys.name: Lists: add, check off, offline replay

steps.text: Add an item with the wall keyboard, check it off, clear checked.
Add an item from a phone.
An item added in one browser shows in another within a second.
A check made before its add returns still lands once the network is back.
Long-press an item to delete it; create and delete a list.
Assign a list to a grown-up or the House; group and filter lists by owner.

journeys.name: Meals plan and saved meals to grocery

steps.text: Plan a dinner; it shows in Meals and on the calendar week.
Edit or delete a planned meal.
Save a meal, add its ingredients to Grocery, plan a day from it.
A meal edited offline is saved once back online.
Meals fit a phone with no sideways scroll.
Saved meal writes need a grown-up; reading and adding to Grocery do not.

journeys.name: Photo frame slideshow and sleep schedule

steps.text: When idle the wall returns Home, then starts the photo frame; a touch leaves it.
The slideshow plays on its interval, preloads, and fills both photo shapes.
The frame overlay shows the clock, date, weather and next event.
On this day favors past-year photos.
The sleep schedule and Sleep now power the display down and back.
steps.simulated: the screen-power calls are proven against the API; the real panel is only checked on the Pi (hub-xcr)

steps.text: At night the dim, warm clock names the morning's first event; a touch wakes the app.
A grown-up adds photo folders, hides a photo, and sets the interval.
A grown-up connects Google and imports photos with the Google Photos picker.
The photo frame plays Live Photo clips.

journeys.name: Parent sets up the household
journeys.persona: Parent on a phone or iPad

steps.text: A fresh hub shows setup, creates the first grown-up and PIN, then guards the routes.
Add and edit family members.
Unlock with the PIN; five wrong attempts lock it; Lock ends the session.
Create, edit and archive chores, habits, routines and rewards.
Choose wall or personal device, screen direction, idle timers and the sleep schedule.
Choose appearance, sounds, quiet hours and the wave palette.
Pick the household time zone and weather location.
Set up notifications and send a test.
Export all data as JSON; a bad import is refused.
Every admin page and form fits a phone without sideways scroll.
Pick a playlist; it plays with big controls and pause.
steps.simulated: Spotify and the Pi speaker are fakes in the tests

steps.text: Volume stops at the parent cap.
An asleep speaker shows a sheet and Try again starts the music.
A grown-up connects Spotify, curates playlists and sets limits.
A grown-up changes the speaker: scan, pair, test sound.
Open Timers from Home and start one.
Pause, add a minute, cancel; the pill follows along.
A finished timer shows a banner and sounds the alarm until dismissed.
A kid posts a sticky note without a PIN; an adult pins it; anyone dismisses it.
A note that has expired is gone.
The same flow works on a phone.
Set vacation: the kid board pauses, and ending it restores the jobs.
A grown-up sets and ends vacation from Settings.
The kid sees a streak badge and a milestone banner paid exactly once.
A grown-up adds a game; it shows on the Games tab, opens in a frame, and Back returns.
A game that cannot load shows a friendly message.
The game form warns about home-network addresses but still saves.

journeys.name: Siri shortcuts API
journeys.persona: Parent on a phone or iPad

steps.text: A grown-up makes a Siri token, sees it once, then revokes it.
Siri adds a list item and does a Star Job with the token.
steps.simulated: the Shortcuts app on a real iPhone is not driven; the API is covered by unit tests

steps.text: Every tap target meets 60 px (96 px on kid screens) and nothing sits behind hover.
All wall text is legible and the layout has no overflow in portrait.
Phones and iPads in both orientations fit the shell, clear the safe areas, and avoid input zoom.
Pages have no serious accessibility violations.
Taps and celebrations stay fast.
The hub installs to the Home Screen and the container serves health and shuts down cleanly.
Tap a big Home controls tile: it flips at once and settles with the server.
A failed tap rolls back and says so.
Unreachable Home Assistant is handled gracefully, and the card is hidden when nothing is configured.
A grown-up connects Home Assistant, tests it, picks, renames and reorders entities.
steps.simulated: Home Assistant is a fake server in the tests

steps.text: Draw with a pen or finger on the Home notes card and post it to the board.
Tap a drawing to enlarge it; anyone dismisses it.
A grown-up fills in the info card: emergency contacts, address, allergies, bedtimes, house rules, Wi-Fi and notes for tonight.
Start a sitter session now or on a schedule, with an optional sitter name, 4-digit PIN and permissions.
Extend a session or end it early; it ends itself at its end time.
The wall gets the info card only during an active session, and with a PIN only after the sitter enters it.
The sitter always has the Emergency info button (behind the sitter PIN when one is set), and the parent-only parts of the wall are locked while a session runs.
A parent starts, extends and ends a session from their phone, and the sitter can check in (kids in bed, all good, call me).
After a session, the parents read a short log of the check-ins and when they happened.
When the parents allow it, the sitter checks Star Jobs with the sitter PIN; otherwise approving stays with the parents.
While a session runs the wall's home is tonight's plan: dinner, evening routines, each child's bedtime and when the parents are back, plus the house rules.
